title: prototype an AI-assisted travel-planning application
input: The builder defines a prototype prompt and permitted public travel preferences.
action: PartyRock lets the builder assemble supported generative-AI application widgets and their connections. Widgets generate prototype content from supplied inputs; the prototype does not reserve travel or validate commercial availability.
output: The builder tests the itinerary prototype and decides which behavior needs a separately engineered production backend.
check: Check unsupported claims, sharing visibility and sensitive-input restrictions before distributing the prototype.

title: replace a historical customer-engagement campaign workflow
input: The engagement owner inventories audience segments, consent, event schema and message templates.
action: Pinpoint historically supported engagement segmentation and campaigns under configured channel settings. Migration separates permitted transactional messaging from audience and campaign orchestration in the chosen replacement.
output: The new campaign system selects consented recipients and dispatches approved messages through supported messaging channels.
check: Reconcile consent, suppression lists and delivery outcomes before transferring scheduled campaigns.

title: answer an employee question using authorized enterprise context
input: The employee asks a work question through the organization's configured Q experience.
action: Amazon Q's selected enterprise experience uses configured sources or developer context to assist the user. For enterprise knowledge, retrieval respects the configured identity and document-access integration; generated answers require evidence review.
output: The employee checks cited material and uses the answer to locate the relevant approved procedure.
check: Test a restricted document with allowed and denied users and reject answers unsupported by retrieved evidence.

title: find an internal policy answer without exposing another team's documents
input: The employee signs in through the enterprise application and submits a policy question.
action: Q Business retrieves relevant content from configured, synchronized enterprise sources using the application's identity and access controls, then generates an answer with available citations.
output: The employee follows cited policy sections and escalates an unanswered question to the policy owner.
check: Test source ACL synchronization, stale content and denied-user queries before accepting the search experience.

title: publish a reusable employee request-summary application
input: The employee defines permitted input fields and a supported reusable Q Apps workflow.
action: Q Apps turns the supported task into a reusable application with configured cards and data inputs in Q Business. It uses the allowed enterprise context; business writes require an explicitly supported and authorized action.
output: The employee reviews the generated request summary before submitting it through the actual business process.
check: Verify application sharing, source access and unsupported action behavior using different employee roles.

title: review an assisted code change before deployment
input: The developer supplies an approved repository task and reviews the allowed assistant context.
action: Q Developer assists with supported code understanding, suggestions and development tasks. Proposed edits are applied only within the chosen development workflow; repository tests and review establish release readiness.
output: The developer inspects the diff, runs the build and submits the accepted change through normal pull-request review.
check: Test the changed behavior and check dependency, secret and license policy before promoting assisted code.

service: Amazon Q Developer in chat applications
title: triage an alarm from an authorized chat channel
input: The operations owner connects a supported chat channel and scoped AWS notification or command role.
action: Q Developer in chat applications delivers configured AWS notifications and supports permitted chat interactions or commands. The channel and IAM roles bound operational access; receiving a notification is not remediation.
output: The responder inspects the alarm context and invokes only an approved supported command or opens the incident runbook.
check: Test channel membership, command denial and account selection before allowing production operational actions.

title: publish an authorized sales dashboard
input: The analyst prepares sales data, dataset access and agreed reporting dimensions.
action: QuickSight's configured data-source and dataset layer imports or directly queries the selected sales data. The analysis defines calculations and visuals; row-level and user permissions control dashboard visibility.
output: The sales manager opens the published dashboard and drills into the permitted regional metrics.
check: Reconcile totals with source records and test row-level restrictions using regional viewer accounts.

title: share a sales analysis through a governed dashboard
input: The analyst defines the approved sales dataset, refresh schedule and viewer groups.
action: QuickSight reads or imports the configured data and evaluates the dashboard's selected visual and calculation definitions. Dataset access and row-level rules determine which sales records reach each viewer.
output: The manager reviews authorized sales trends through the published dashboard rather than querying the raw warehouse directly.
check: Validate refresh freshness, calculated totals and cross-region access denial before sharing the dashboard.

title: retain archive objects and restore a selected record
input: The records owner selects the applicable S3 archive storage class and retention requirements.
action: S3 archive storage classes retain objects at the selected archival tier. Classes requiring restoration need an accepted restore request and waiting period before temporary readable access; retrieval behavior depends on the exact class.
output: The records application downloads the restored object and verifies it against the retained manifest.
check: Test retrieval timing, restore expiry, legal retention and checksum integrity for the chosen storage class.
